genxml.title: Alteon Tigon PCI/Gigabit Ethernet controller (SGI IRIS Gigabit Ethernet board)
genxml.doc: Offsets are byte offsets in the chip's PCI memory window, as the manual's register tables give them. Fields are the bit positions the register descriptions name. Grades say how each item was derived: established means read in the Alteon Tigon/PCI Ethernet Controller manual, revision 1.04; inferred means a public driver's use or a reading the manual does not state. Reset values come only from the manual's reset statements. Nothing here was measured on a board. The prose and the sources the register rules rest on are in devices/tigon/README.md.

struct.name: MISC_HOST_CTL
struct.doc: Miscellaneous Host Control. The read-write bits sit in the low byte, so a host that writes a byte-wide No Swap value can copy that byte into every lane. The manual gives no reset value for this register.

struct.name: PCI_STATE
struct.doc: PCI State. All bits are zero at reset. The Miscellaneous Host Control reset does not change this register. Bit 20 and the bits under it are the ones the host-bus rules turn on.

struct.name: DMA_WRITE_STATE
struct.doc: DMA Write State, the state of the write channel that moves data from the card to the host. The manual gives no reset value.

struct.name: DMA_READ_STATE
struct.doc: DMA Read State, the state of the read channel that moves data from the host to the card. The manual gives no reset value.

struct.name: MAILBOX_0_LOW
struct.doc: Word of mailbox 0 that raises the mailbox event, read as the least significant word at the higher address. Inferred: the manual contradicts itself. Section 2.7 says a write to the upper half of one of the 32 eight-byte locations raises the event, and section 9.12.3 says a write to the least significant word does and a write to the most significant word does not. The Linux driver writes its producer indexes to the words at offset 4 of each location, which matches 9.12.3 if the least significant word sits at the higher address. Writing mailbox 0 also deasserts the PCI interrupt pin at once, so a host can clear the interrupt and pass a message in one write. The manual says a mailbox may be read back as often as needed. The same word of mailbox n is eight bytes after that of mailbox n minus one.
